items.claim: The couplet's cross-verse recurrence claim is left untiered where the byte tier is exact, and the second English run is presented without the mandatory curly delimiter, with a source curly mark rendered straight inside it.
items.evidence: The repeated address is byte-identical across the two verses: אַל תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ (oshb:Jer.46.28, byte) is the same four-token run at oshb:Jer.46.27 (byte), the sole divergence being the conjunction on the opening word (וְ֠אַתָּה at oshb:Jer.46.27, byte, against אַ֠תָּה at oshb:Jer.46.28, byte). Calling that "nearly verbatim" without naming the tier leaves a recurrence claim untiered exactly where byte-tier truth is available and exact, and it understates the evidence for the row's own cohesion. Second, the English run for web:Jer.46.28 is the only one of the forty-two English runs in this cluster that opens with no curly delimiter (sweep: 1 of 42 runs): it begins bare, and the folded WEB text's curly closing mark after the servant address is rendered as a straight double quote inside a verbatim run, so the curly-quote-plus-inline-ref pairing required of every WEB citation is broken for that run. What verifies: the addressee shift at 46:27 to a comfort address to Jacob is byte-true and is a tier-1 class; both in-span setumot (46:27, 46:28) and the in-span paseq (46:28) are disclosed with single-witness language at the right verses; the preceding setumah at 46:26 is cited correctly; the span carries no ketiv/qere; 46:28 is the last verse of the chapter in both witnesses (28 verses each), so the chapter-close statement holds; and the type deviation to a salvation reading inside the header-bounded nations block is disclosed per the operative-category allowance.

items.claim: The header's dating element is labeled a relative clause in two fields, but its bytes are a temporal clause, and the verse's only relative particle heads the header shape itself.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.47.1 dates the header with בְּטֶ֛רֶם יַכֶּ֥ה (oshb:Jer.47.1, byte) - beterem plus a prefix-conjugation verb, a temporal subordinate clause, matching “before Pharaoh struck Gaza” (web:Jer.47.1). The single relative particle in the verse, אֲשֶׁ֨ר (oshb:Jer.47.1, byte), opens the asher-hayah header itself, so the label both misassigns the form class and, read literally, would attach the header's own particle to the date. A form-class label is a byte-checkable claim carrying the same discipline as a digit, and this row asserts it twice - in the rationale and again in the device note - at high confidence. What verifies: 47:1 is one of the four verses carrying the asher-hayah debar-YHWH el-Yirmeyahu header shape (sweep: 4 verses), and 46:1, cited as the collection rubric, is another; the divine-speech formula at 47:2 stands on the divine mouth, not a quoted human one, and correctly only sets this frame rather than changing an established one; both in-span setumot (47:1, 47:5) and the in-span paseq (47:2) are disclosed with single-witness language; the preceding setumah at 46:28 is cited correctly; no ketiv/qere falls in the span; and every Hebrew run in the row reaches byte tier at its cited verse.

items.claim: The sword-apostrophe onset, the addressee reading, the chapter close, and the mark disclosure are all byte-true, and the row does not overreach its tier-3 corroboration.
items.evidence: The onset token ה֗וֹי (oshb:Jer.47.6, byte) stands verse-initial (skeleton offset 0), and the imperatives following it are directed at the sword rather than at a nation or person, matching “You sword of Yahweh, how long will it be before you are quiet?” (web:Jer.47.6). Typing it as a sword apostrophe rather than a woe onset or a funeral cry matches the byte-derived role split, which holds this site in its own class apart from the woe onsets at 22:13 and 23:1 and the vav-prefixed funeral shapes; the row makes the role split before any digit, as required. Chapter 47 ends at verse 7 in both witnesses (7 verses each), so the claim that the closing mark ends both row and chapter holds. The in-span setumah at 47:7 and the preceding setumah at 47:5 are both disclosed as single-witness and explicitly denied driver status; the span carries no paseq and no ketiv/qere, and none is claimed. The next-unit header quoted at 48:1 is the lamed-initial Moab header, byte-true and correctly not reached.

items.evidence: 48:1 is a lamed-initial nation header, and the woe token ה֤וֹי (oshb:Jer.48.1, byte) sits mid-verse inside that header rather than verse-initial (skeleton offset 35 of 100), which is exactly the woe-inside-header role the byte-derived inventory records for this site and distinct from the bare verse-initial woe onsets elsewhere; the row discloses it as such instead of blending it into a woe count. The full divine-title stack יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.48.1, byte) also stands at oshb:Jer.46.25 (byte), and the cited digit is right as an object and a unit (sweep: 32 verses for the full stack, counted separately from bare tsevaot). All three ketiv/qere verses in the span are disclosed in the correct written-against-read direction - 48:4, 48:5, and the doubled 48:7 - and the doubled site is described as one of the twelve without asserting an ordinal. No paragraph mark falls in the span; the preceding setumah at 47:7 is cited correctly and held as tier-3 single-witness texture. items.claim: The exclusivity guarding the deceit-noun splice is asserted in words with no digit, and the imperative used as this row's onset is the same unnamed-addressee shape the unit ending at 48:8 refused as a seam.
items.evidence: The splice רְמִיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.48.10, byte) is genuinely unique as a token - a token-bound sweep returns 1 verse - while a bare consonantal substring sweep for the same skeleton returns 118 verses because the prophet's name contains it. The row states that uniqueness only in words ("the single attested token at this one site", "every occurrence of the prophet's own name") and carries neither digit; an exclusivity claim about a swept object may not rest on wording, and here the two digits that actually make the point (1 verse token-bound against 118 verses as a substring) exist and are omitted. Second, the onset warrant: תְּנוּ (oshb:Jer.48.9, byte) is a plural imperative with no named addressee, Moab standing in the third person through the rest of the verse, yet the unit ending at 48:8 declined a cut at נֻ֖סוּ מַלְּט֣וּ (oshb:Jer.48.6, byte) on the stated ground that the imperative carries no named vocative addressee of its own. The same byte feature therefore both does and does not make a seam eight verses apart, leaving the distinction to a change of figure rather than to a device the bytes mark. What verifies: the twofold curse at 48:10 is byte-true, the in-span setumah at 48:11 is disclosed and correctly held as texture rather than a sub-boundary against the connective binding 48:11 to 48:12, the formula at 48:12 does sit mid-verse rather than verse-final, and every Hebrew run reaches byte tier.

items.claim: The melekh-signature identification, its ordinal, its placement contrast, and the closure-corroboration reasoning are all byte-true, and the calibration matches the honestly disclosed judgment call.
items.evidence: The signature נְאֻ֨ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.48.15, byte) occurs in exactly three verses (sweep: 3 verses: 46:18, 48:15, 51:57), so both "second of three" and the citation of 46:18 as the first are correct, and the digit names its object and unit. The placement contrast is byte-accurate: at 48:15 the run closes the verse (skeleton offset 42, running to the end), while at 46:18 it stands after חַי אָ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.46.18, byte) inside the oath with the verse continuing past it (offset 7 of 61). The row claims the same construction rather than byte identity across sites, which is the correct strength: the two sites agree at skeleton tier and differ in accentuation. The onset at 48:14 is a second-person plural address enclosing a quoted boast, byte-true; 48:16 carries no formula, vocative, or woe, so declining to let the signature close the row there follows the closure rule rather than bending it. Calibration is right: medium_low with the frontier flag set, and the attachment of 48:16 to this row rather than to the mourning summons at 48:17 disclosed as a genuine judgment call. No paragraph mark, paseq, or ketiv/qere falls in the span, and none is claimed.

items.claim: 48:20 is called the second of the book's twelve doubled ketiv/qere verses, but in that inventory it stands eighth.
items.evidence: Ordered by chapter and verse, the book's multi-note ketiv/qere verses are 3:19, 4:19, 6:25, 13:20, 14:14, 22:23, 48:7, 48:20, 49:39, 50:6, 50:11 and 51:34 (12 verses). 48:20 is the eighth member and 48:7, cited earlier in this same cluster, is the seventh; only a chapter-scoped reading would make 48:20 "second", and the sentence scopes the set explicitly to the book. This is a digit-class claim against a byte-derived inventory in the campaign's largest disclosure layer, so it cannot stand as written; the cure is to drop the ordinal, as the 48:7 disclosure already does. What verifies: the ketiv/qere at 48:18 and both pairs at 48:20 are given in the correct written-against-read direction and collate at byte tier inside their verses; the paseq at 48:20 is cited count-only with no intra-verse position; the scene is byte-true as three addressees - a plural summons to the neighbors at 48:17, then singular addresses to Dibon at 48:18 and to Aroer at 48:19, both carrying yod-final imperative forms and rendered as direct address in both witnesses - closing on the summary proclamation at 48:20; and no paragraph mark falls in the span, with none claimed.

items.claim: The form contrast at this row's own seams leans on translation-layer poetry-line metadata, states it inaccurately, and names the staged data key in prose; and the reading of the next verse as carrying no tier-1 onset conflicts with the imperative-onset warrant used at 48:9.
items.evidence: The device note offers the span's poetry-line counts as "at or near zero throughout" and makes that a texture distinguishing this span from the scene before it and the scene after it. Modern poetry-line breaks are translation-layer metadata that is never boundary evidence and never counterevidence in either direction, so this cannot do seam-distinguishing work even as texture; and the figure is not accurate as stated - across 48:21-25 the folded WEB counts run 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, against 3, 4, 2, 3 across 48:17-20 and 3 at 48:26, which is a relative contrast, not a run at or near zero. The underlying data key also surfaces verbatim in row prose. Separately, the rationale states that no fresh tier-1 onset follows immediately at 48:26, but that verse opens הַשְׁכִּירֻ֕הוּ (oshb:Jer.48.26, byte), a plural imperative of the same discourse-frame class this row's neighbor at 48:9 uses as its own onset driver; the statement therefore misclassifies the device and, in doing so, understates the row's own closing warrant, since the closing formula would then be valid corroboration rather than merely disclosed. What verifies: the town list really is joined by repeated conjunctions in the bytes with no verbal frame between the names, the ketiv/qere at 48:21 is disclosed in the correct written-against-read direction, the closing formula at 48:25 does stand verse-final, and no paragraph mark or paseq falls in the span.
